source: Belfield, S. and Brown, C. (2010). Guidebook on Upland Crops in Cambodia: Corn (សៀវភៅណែនាំ ស្តីពីដំណាំតំបន់ខ្ពង់រាបនៅក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា៖ ដំណាំពោត). ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. text:
Corn production in Cambodia's main upland corn-growing provinces in 2004-05 (MAFF Cambodia 2004-05):

- Banteay Meanchey: white corn 10,489 tonnes (2% of national white corn production); yellow corn 10,082 tonnes (5% of national yellow corn production).
- Battambang: white corn 155,030 tonnes (32% of national white corn production); yellow corn 150,406 tonnes (67% of national yellow corn production).
- Pailin: white corn 43,354 tonnes (9% of national white corn production); yellow corn 43,151 tonnes (19% of national yellow corn production).
- Combined (these three provinces): white corn 208,873 tonnes (43% of national white corn production); yellow corn 203,642 tonnes (91% of national yellow corn production).

This shows that Battambang and Pailin together dominate Cambodia's yellow (commercial/feed) corn production -- these two provinces alone account for the large majority of national yellow corn output -- while white (glutinous/eating) corn production is comparatively more dispersed across the country, with these three upland provinces accounting for less than half of the national white corn total.
